Breast Cancer Awareness Month.
As the Mayor of Montebello, I stand
before you this evening to recognize a
cause that deeply affects so many
families across our nation. Breast
Cancer Awareness Month.
Each October, we come together under the
symbol of pink ribbons to raise
awareness, support early detection, and
honor the courage of those who have
faced breast cancer. It's a time to
stand with survivors, remember those
that we have lost, and offer strength to
the families and loved ones.
In 2026, an estimate of 321,910
women and 2,670
men in the United States will be
diagnosed with invasive breast cancer.
Sadly, approximately 42,670
lives are expected to be lost to this
disease.
Breast cancer remains the second leading
cause of cancer-related
deaths among women and approximately 1/8
one in eight women will develop invasive
breast cancer during their lifetime.
These numbers remind us why we
why continued education, early
detection, regular screenings, and
advancement in research are so critical.
Here in Montebello, we reaffirm our
commitment to promoting health and
wellness, encouraging access to prevent
care, and support those affected at
every stage of their journey.
Together, let's continue to spread
awareness, to encourage regular
screenings, and offer compassion and
hope to everyone impacted by this
disease. To learn more about breast
cancer awareness, support those
affected, and contribute to the research
for a cure, you can visit National
Breast Cancer Foundation at www.
.nationalbreastcancer.org.
We also have domestic violence awareness
month.
October is also recognized as domestic
violence awareness month,
a time to raise our collective voice
against a devastating issue that
continues to affect individuals and
families in communities across our
nation.
Domestic violence takes many forms. It's
physical, emotional, psychological,
financial, or digital, and impacts
people of all backgrounds regardless of
age, gender, or circumstance.
It is a serious issue that threatens
personal safety,
disrupts families, and can have a
lasting effect on survivors and their
loved ones.
Raising awareness and helping
individuals recognize the warning signs
of abuse are important steps toward
prevention.
Here in Montebello, we remain committed
to promoting education, prevention, and
access to resources that help survivors
find safety and support.
We also recognize the difficult and
often dangerous work performed by our
law enforcement officers, victim
advocates, and community service
providers who respond to these
situations, assist survivors, and help
families rebuild their lives.
This month, let us reaffirm our
commitment to creating a community
rooted in respect,
compassion,
equality, and safety for all. Together,
we can break the cycle of abuse, empower
survivors, and support those working
every day to prevent domestic violence.
October also recognizes National Bully
Prevention Month, a time to come
together as a community to stand against
bullying in all forms and promote
kindness, acceptance, and respect.
Bullying, whether verbal or physical,
social, or online, can have lasting
effects on a person's confidence,
safety, and mental well-being.
While social media and digital
communication play an increasing
significant role in our daily daily
lives, addressing cyberbullying and
educating young people about responsible
online behavior have become more
important than ever.
Here in Montebello, we recognize the
importance of programs and partnerships
that help foster kindness, leadership,
and inclusion
among our youth and adults alike. Our
schools, recreational centers, families,
and community organizations all play an
important role in ensuring Montebello
remains a place where everyone feels
valued, respected, and safe.
This month and every month, we encourage
all residents to take a stance against
bullying, to speak up when they witness
harmful behavior, support those who may
be struggling, and lead by example
through acts of kindness and
understanding. Together, we can make
Montebello a community where everybody
can thrive without fear or intimidation.
